A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AttWarp work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark accuracies, ablations, robustness analyses and appendix experiments, including open-vocabulary object detection.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, attention-layer sensitivity, warping-intensity measurements and classifier-gating results.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 adds AttWarp†, a learned binary gate deciding whether to apply warping. It reuses AttWarp-Distill with a classifier head replacing its last two layers. The core AttWarp, AttWarp-Chain and AttWarp-Distill procedures are otherwise retained.

E1.justification: V3 adds evaluations on MMVP, single-image BLINK, RealWorldQA and MIA-Bench. These extend coverage to CLIP-blind visual discrimination, additional perceptual and spatial challenges, and constrained multimodal instruction following. The original five benchmarks and appendix gRef/OVOD coverage remain.

E2.justification: Figure 7 adds AttWarp + Classifier to the existing base-MLLM/AttWarp error comparison. The FGVP-mask/blur, SoM, API and ViCrop comparator sets remain unchanged in matched experiments. New Table 2 uses the already evaluated base LLaVA comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix G.1 changes the reported MMMU attention transform from square root to identity, without establishing that the unchanged scores were rerun. Added protocols specify individual-question MMVP accuracy, single-image BLINK, deeper-layer controls and a Jacobian-based diagnostic. The added layer index is inconsistent: Table 4 says 22, whereas Appendix B.1 says 24.

E4.justification: V3 adds accuracy-based attention-layer sensitivity across two backbones and five benchmarks (Table 4), warping intensity by question type (Table 12), and classifier gating in the retained 150-example error study (Figure 7). New failure examples show warping introducing a size error and failing on clothing recognition, substantially extending the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Run-count, seed and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. Both versions report point-estimate accuracies and retain the same random-head resampling description and FID/KID estimation setup; v3 introduces no confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds four-benchmark results; for example, Table 2 reports MMVP accuracies of 48.3 for base LLaVA, 50.7 for AttWarp and 51.0 for AttWarp-Chain. New layer, intensity and gating results include size errors decreasing from 17 to 13 with gating. Table 1 retains its raw accuracies but rebases deltas from the best prior method to the base MLLM, explaining changes such as +4.0 to +11.0 on LLaVA TextVQA.

T1.justification: Equation 3 corrects the vertical inverse-CDF subscript from Mx to My. Appendix C.3 introduces mean log-change of Jacobian determinants as a warping-intensity definition. Existing mathematical formulations are otherwise retained; Appendix J primarily interprets the existing resampling operation rather than introducing a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the claimed empirical scope from five to nine benchmarks. The central contribution remains improving frozen MLLMs through context-preserving rectilinear warping. The new self-correction terminology mainly reframes the already described attention-and-warp loop.

C2.justification: Appendix J interprets AttWarp as reallocating a fixed visual-token budget and Distill as predicting a patch grid. Appendix C.3 explains global-context gains through milder warping, while B.1 adds a broader deep-layer robustness interpretation. Section 4.3 explains that classifier gating cannot repair attention misalignment shared by the base model and AttWarp.

D1.justification: V3 documents the classifier's initialization, head replacement and outcome-based training-data construction. Appendix G.1 changes reported hardware from four 16GB V100 GPUs to eight A100s and revises the MMMU transform. The abstract now explicitly describes code and demos as available through the existing project page.

R1.justification: V3 adds benchmark references for BLINK, MMVP, MIA-Bench and RealWorldQA. Section 2 repositions the already cited Mao et al. (2025) as contemporaneous magnification work. The broader related-work organization and contribution positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording edits, adds the ICLR publication header and reorders portions of Section 4.2. Former Appendix D.5 moves to E.3, and new C.3/J sections add explanatory material. The main narrative and section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 2, 4 and 12, redraws Figure 7 with a third bar series and new failure panels, and revises Figure 3 labels and Table 1's caption. Figure 12 reorders retained OVOD examples but incorrectly labels the girl-holding-a-bear example as 'Man in black facing us'. Most other displays are retained or reflowed.

improvement.justification: V3 broadens empirical support through additional perceptual, spatial and instruction-following evaluations, while the layer, warping-intensity and gating analyses improve understanding of applicability and failures. These gains are limited by comparisons only against base LLaVA on the new benchmarks and new reporting errors, notably the layer-22/table versus layer-24/prose mismatch and Figure 12's incorrect query label.
